text.p: Owens Corning and Fibreboard Corp said Thursday the waiting period imposed by federal regulators on their previously announced merger has expired.
The companies said Owens Corning has proceeded with its tender offer to acquire all outstanding shares of Fibreboard at $55 per share. The total value of the deal is estimated at $515 million.
Fibreboard is among the nation's biggest producers of vinyl siding. Its purchase is expected to make Owens Corning, a recent addition to that market, a major industry force.
The merger is expected to be accretive to Owens Corning in 1997 and on an ongoing basis, the companies said. The companies expect the transaction to close early in the third quarter of 1997.

Headquartered in Toledo, Ohio, Owens Corning produces high performance glass fiber composites and building materials with sales in 1996 of $3.8 billion. The company employs 19,000 people in more than 30 countries.

Dallas-based Fibreboard had sales in 1996 of $469 million. On a pro-forma basis the company's sales this year would be expected to be close to $800 million, the companies said. The company employs 3,400 people and operates a total of 21 manufacturing plants in the United States and Canada.
